name: Summit Peaks Resorts
blurb: Public ski company, six mountains, one season pass. Founder Dana Strand built it from a single hill in Alder Creek and holds 30% of the vote. Alder Creek is the oldest mountain and the town's main employer.

directors.name: Marisa Kell
directors.title: Attorney
directors.motive: Your firm has handled Summit's lift contracts for years, and you wrote the memo calling the inspection schedule advisory. You are no longer sure that word will hold up.

exposure.text: You are disbarred if the board is caught hiding a heavy fact.
exposure.label: Disbarred if caught hiding

secrets.text: Clean the books: the board admits every fact in round 1.
secrets.label: Admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Your firm bills Summit $2M a year. One caught fact ends it, so none may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Tomas Reyes
directors.title: Labor director
directors.motive: Your members run the lifts, so you know what a worn cable sounds like. You also know that closing a lift in January costs the crew its hours.

exposure.text: Members vote you out if the pension payment is skipped.
exposure.label: Pension skipped

secrets.text: Chair 7 closes for inspection before anyone gets hurt.
secrets.label: Chair 7 closes

secrets.text: Your members' pension fund holds Summit stock. The stock must end above where it started.
secrets.label: Stock ends above start

directors.name: Grace Whitlow
directors.title: Fund partner
directors.motive: Granite Peak backed Summit at a price that assumed every lift running all season. You do not want to be the investor who closed one, or the one who left it open.

exposure.text: Your investors pull their money if the stock ends below where it started.
exposure.label: Stock ends below start

secrets.text: Granite Peak also lent Summit money, and the loan terms hold only if every lift runs. Chair 7 must stay open.
secrets.label: Chair 7 stays open

secrets.text: Your fund quietly owns a rival ski company. The stock must finish in the bottom half.
secrets.label: Stock ends in bottom half

directors.name: Hal Brennan
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.motive: Dana shared a dorm room with you and a business plan on a napkin. SnowSense is her new bet and she needs the pension money to fund it.

exposure.text: You lose the seat if the board votes down skipping the pension payment, which Dana wants.
exposure.label: Pension skip voted down

secrets.text: Dana signed off on delaying the Chair 7 inspection. The board must never admit every fact about it in round 1.
secrets.label: Don't admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: SnowSense is Dana's pet project and needs the cash. The pension payment must be skipped.
secrets.label: Pension skipped

directors.name: June Okafor
directors.title: Community seat (Mayor)
directors.motive: Alder Creek is where Summit began, and half your voters work a lift or a bar that depends on one. You live beside Chair 7 and wave at the people riding it.

exposure.text: You face a recall if the board is caught hiding a fact.
exposure.label: Caught hiding

secrets.text: The pension is paid in full.
secrets.label: Pension paid

secrets.text: Your family owns the lodge beside Chair 7, and a January closure would cost it the holiday weekend. Chair 7 stays open.
secrets.label: Chair 7 stays open

motions.title: Close Chair 7 until it is inspected
motions.motive: Better a dark lift than a bad day.

headline.passed: Summit Peaks shuts Chair 7 for inspection

issue.text: Chair 7's yearly safety inspection is 14 months overdue and a technician logged wear on one cable. The maker says the wear may be within limits. Nothing has gone wrong, and safety reports go to operations, not the board.
issue.case_for_silence: Nothing has failed, the wear may be within limits, and a public warning could empty the mountain over a holiday weekend.

facts.text: Chair 7's yearly safety inspection is 14 months overdue.
A technician logged wear on a cable, and the maker says it may still be within limits.
Operations knew in March, and safety reports go to operations, not to the board.
The crew that maintains the lift also signs off on its inspection.

motions.title: Skip this year's pension payment
motions.motive: Probably legal. The fund will recover when the markets do.

headline.passed: Summit Peaks skips this year's pension payment
headline.failed: Summit Peaks board pays the pension in full

issue.text: The staff pension is about $60M short under this year's estimate, though two actuaries disagree on the size. Counsel says skipping is probably legal. Staff statements still call the fund secure.
issue.case_for_silence: The estimate is contested, counsel says skipping is probably legal, and a scare about the pension could send your best crew to other mountains.

facts.text: Under this year's estimate the staff pension is about $60M short.
Staff statements still describe the pension as secure.
The board has been told the gap could widen if markets stay down.
Counsel says skipping a payment this year is probably legal.

cases.line: Boeing had no board safety committee until 2019, and its directors settled oversight claims for $237.5M.
Hostess stopped paying into its bakers' pension in 2011, calling it temporary. It went bankrupt in January 2012 and later shut down.

real.fix: Give safety and pension risk a committee that hears bad news directly.
